title: Expressions
description: Write, simplify, and evaluate algebraic expressions.

lessons.title: What is a Variable?
objectives: Understand variables as symbols for unknown values

pedagogy.title: A variable is a placeholder
pedagogy.content: Think of a variable as a box that can hold any number.

content.content: A variable is a letter that represents an unknown or changing quantity. If $x$ stands for the number of apples, then $x + 5$ means 5 more apples.

exercises.question: Write an expression for 'a number $n$ increased by 7'.
Write an expression for 'the product of 4 and a number $x$'.

pedagogy.title: Combine like terms
pedagogy.content: Terms with the same variable part can be combined by adding their coefficients.

content.content: Like terms have the same variable raised to the same power. $3x$ and $5x$ are like terms; $3x$ and $3x^2$ are not.

exercises.question: Simplify $2x + 3y + 5x - y$.
exercises.solution: $2x + 5x = 7x$ and $3y - y = 2y$, so the simplified expression is $7x + 2y$.

exercises.question: Simplify $3(x + 4)$.
hints: Multiply 3 by each term inside the parentheses.

lessons.title: Evaluating Expressions
objectives: Substitute values into expressions and simplify

pedagogy.title: Use parentheses
pedagogy.content: When substituting a negative number or a fraction, use parentheses to avoid sign errors.

content.content: To evaluate an expression, replace each variable with its given value and simplify.
